doc.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

title: Embarrassing record dates
summary: Humiliations on recordings and a rough count of about 70 records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: What’s the worst scrape you ever got into? Can you recall?

I can’t really think about it. I mean I can think of some scenes I had with various musicians but nothing — I mean I can think of humiliations I suffered, of my own making. Like this one record I was on I would love to burn. I won’t tell you what it was. Two actually. I just — one I hadn’t touched a piano for like three weeks or something and I went up there thinking I don’t have to play and they called me up to play and I was all thumbs.
But they put it out anyway of course.
They put it out anyway. So I’ve been about 70 or so records I guess.
